title: Possessive Adjectives
objectives: Use my, your, his, her, its, our, their before nouns.
canDo: I can use possessive adjectives to say who owns something.

warmUp.title: Posse
warmUp.prompt: Como dizemos "meu livro", "seu carro", "a casa deles" em inglês?
reflectionQuestions: What is the difference between he and his?

explanation:
Possessive adjectives show ownership. They come BEFORE a noun.

my (meu/minha) | your (seu/sua) | his (dele) | her (dela) | its (de algo) | our (nosso) | their (deles)

Example: This is my phone. That is her bag.

Do NOT use articles with possessives: ✗ the my book → ✓ my book

grammar.title: Possessive Adjectives
grammar.rule: Possessive adjectives replace articles before nouns: my book, her car. Match the owner: his = a man/boy, her = a woman/girl, their = plural.

sentences: No, it is not my umbrella. It is her umbrella.

reading.title: Whose Is This?
reading.text: In the classroom, the teacher finds three items: a blue pen, a red notebook, and a green water bottle. "Whose pen is this?" she asks. Marco says: "It is my pen." Lucia says: "The notebook is her notebook — it has Sofia's name." The water bottle is their water bottle — Tom and Ana share it.

questions.question: Whose pen is it?
questions.explanation: Marco says it is my pen.

questions.question: Whose notebook is it?
questions.explanation: Lucia says it is her notebook — Sofia's name.

questions.question: Do Tom and Ana share the bottle?

writing.prompt: Describe 4 things you and your family have. Use my, his, her, our, or their.
writing.modelAnswer: My laptop is old. My sister's room is big — her room is blue. Our car is white. Their apartment is near the park.

tutorHints: Contrast she/her and he/his on the board.
